text:
anika: quick q — when a runtime config change modifies routing weights + quotas we currently show a delta preview in console. but ops wants a way to simulate the live 'drain' effect and estimated quota burn before applying. any objections to adding a dry-run that runs against a sampled shadow traffic window?
lee: would be helpful. current preview is just diffs, no cost/latency impact estimates. :+1:
maya: important for Dedicated customers — they want to see how quotas move across pools. can we show per-pool token estimate + % of requests that would shift to a different latency tier?
zach: technically doable if we replay a small traffic slice and run the routing decision logic. two caveats: 1) we need consistent prefix/KV cache state to make latency estimates meaningful, 2) privacy — must not send PII to the dry-run service.
anika: good points. assume we use hashed, anonymized keys and only run on internal sampling queue. sample size configurable (default 1%)
jordan: UX thought — surface a small timeline: before/after, delta in token/sec, delta in p95, and a confidence interval. include a flag to 'simulate KV warmup' vs 'cold start' since customers care about both.
lee: what about quotas? for a config change that increases route weight, we should estimate per-route quota consumption and flag possible quota exhaustion within 24h/7d windows. ops-bot can add alerts if estimated burn > threshold.
ops-bot: I can create a runbook hook. would trigger if simulated 24h burn >= 80% of quota. need an RBAC toggle for console users.
maya: console UX: add a small inline 'simulate' button next to the preview diff. modal shows sampled run results, with links to the telemetry traces and a CSV export.
zach: implementation note: reuse routing service's decision function as a library. run in sandbox with a read-only view of config and historical telemetry. we should mark simulated runs in logs to avoid confusing audit trails.
anika: audit question — simulated runs must not be treated as config apply events. keep separate telemetry index 'simulate.*'.
jordan: we should also log whether the simulation used cached prefixes or not and show both numbers side-by-side. that answers the warmup vs steady-state question.
lee: perf question — if someone picks a 10% sample over a large date range, the simulation could be heavy. propose we limit interactive modal runs to a max of 10m or 100k events, then offer a batch job for longer runs.
amika: (typo) meant anika ^
zach: agree. interactive = quick heuristics + small sample. longer batch job queued to infra, with email/console notification when done.
maya: security — ensure KMS keys used by the simulator are customer-scoped for Private deployments. hosted preview can use internal keys with data redaction.
lee: API change: add POST /configs/:id/simulate with body { sample_pct, window_start, window_end, kv_warmup: boolean }. returns job id or inline result if small.
jordan: also allow POST /configs/:id/simulate?dry_run=true for quick inline. include `explain=true` to return routing decision traces for a few sample requests.
anika: can someone sketch minimal telemetry fields we need in simulation result? I'd like a short list to add to console design.
zach: minimal: total_requests_sampled, requests_shifted_by_route (map route->count), estimated_tokens_burned_per_route, p50/p95 latency delta per-route, cache_hit_rate_change, simulated_warmup_flag, simulated_window_start/end, confidence_bound_percentile.
lee: add quota_alerts: [ {route, estimated_burn, quota, percent_of_quota} ] and an overall status: OK/WARN/FAIL.
maya: add a small human summary at top: "Estimated to increase cost by ~X% and shift Y% traffic to slower pools."
anika: perfect. next: who implements API + console? zach for service shim, lee for quota math, jordan for UX, maya to own product sign-off. I'll draft a quick spec and PR.
zach: I'll start a prototype lib to run the decision fn in-process. aim for a spike by EOW.
lee: will draft quota sim math and thresholds.
jordan: will wire mockups into console prototype.
maya: will schedule a 30m sync if needed.
anika: thanks all. filing follow-up PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/proposals/pull/92 (WIP) :eyes:
lee: :shipit: on the plan, let's keep the simulation opt-in for private customers until we validate data hygiene.
zach: will add flags and an escape hatch to disable simulation per-org.
anika: closing loop — will update thread when PR lands. thanks!
